intro.text:
TTP Shop · seasonal shelf · 2026-10-29

Three directions for a dated shelf whose first tenant is Halloween 2026 (Spooky Snouts) and whose next is a winter set. Each row is one direction, left to right: shop landing · the set · preview/try-on · buy · owned/equip · after the window.

Shared facts on every board: the window is a row (key, title, opens_at, closes_at); 'leaving in N days' is computed from closes_at; new pieces are sold only inside the window; the four returning pieces (Skull Mask, Pumpkin Patch, Firefly Lantern, Candy Land) keep their daily-drop life after it. Prices sit in the rarity bands. Balance 1,840 snouts. Costumes are out of scope (no body slot yet).

Art: the Halloween shop art folders were empty at build time, so every Halloween piece on these boards is the trading-card art from assets/images/trading-cards/halloween-2026 as a stand-in; existing items use their shipped sprites. Rosie is sprites/rosie/idle_1 at rest (the shop preview rule). Overlay placement is eyeballed, not the renderer's RelSpec.

Tokens are copied by hand from constants/theme.ts: the 'Tickle the Pig' design system artifact existed but was still empty when this was built.

titleB.text: B · The Pop-up Stall: a card on the wall, a page of its own

titleC.text: C · Dress for the Night: try the look, buy the look

stickyA.text:
A · The Third Plank  (≈ 2.5 h, fits)

What it is: a third plank in the store's wall, above Today's drop, with bunting and a 'leaving in N days' kicker. Three coasters a day from the set (same daily hash as the drop, seeded by shelf key) and an 'all 16 ›' tag that opens the set as a sheet: segment New · Back for the weekend, the shipped 2-col ShopCard grid. Preview is today's ItemPreviewModal plus one lilac tag (leaving in N days). Buy is today's one-tap Buy now (the sheet is the confirm). Owned coasters say Wear / Wearing and dress her in one tap (the 2026-09-17 rule, unchanged). After closes_at the plank stays bare for 3 days with 'back next year', then unmounts.

Pillar fit: Collect (a shelf you can miss is a reason to come back this week); Connect only via the counter (a crewmate's seasonal buy shows there like any buy). Nothing new to learn: one grammar, sun price = on the shelf now.

Vs today: + SeasonalShelf (plank + sign + 3 ShelfItems), + SeasonalSetSheet (Sheet + SegmentedControl + ShopCard grid), + leaving tag in the preview, + shelf ids in buyableIds, + 'leaving in' copy. No route, no new card grammar.

Server: seasonal_shelves(key pk, title, kicker, opens_at, closes_at) + hats.shelf_key, hats.shelf_lane ('new'|'returning'); seasonal_shelf() RPC returns the open shelf + its hats; daily_shop() excludes lane='new' rows; buy_hat() refuses lane='new' outside the window (reason not_in_window). Seed: 1 shelf row, 12 new hats (art paths), 4 returning hats tagged. Winter = one shelf row + its hats, no code.

Hours: migration + seed 0.75 · hook/util + buyable gate 0.5 · plank 0.5 · set sheet 0.5 · preview tag + closed state + tests 0.25 ≈ 2.5. First cut if late: the set sheet ('all 16 ›' scrolls the catalog filtered to the shelf instead).

stickyB.text:
B · The Pop-up Stall  (≈ 3.5 h, over by an hour; a 2.5 h cut exists)

What it is: a painted stall card at the top of the wall (the set's hero background, Rosie in a piece, the countdown) that opens its own route /shop/shelf/[key]. The page is a small store: hero stage that tries on whatever you tap (free, ephemeral), a haul meter (3 of 16), a segment New · Back · Yours, the 2-col grid, Buy on a strip under the hero. Buy confirms with a ConfirmDialog that names the price and the window. After closes_at the card is a boarded sign and the page is an EmptyState with 'Your haul' under it.

Pillar fit: Collect (the set is a place with a meter, so completing it is legible); Connect via the share-ready hero (not drawn: a later step). Contend: none.

Vs today: + stall card, + a pushed route with PageHeader back, + in-place try-on on a stage (PigStage frozen at rest, equip state local to the page), + ProgressTrack haul, + ConfirmDialog on buy (today has none), + segment with Yours. Two preview grammars in the app (sheet elsewhere, stage here): the honest cost of this direction.

Server: same as A plus seasonal_shelves.backdrop_hat_id + theme (title colour, bunting), and seasonal_shelf() returns owned_count. buy_hat() window check identical. Winter = one shelf row.

Hours: migration + seed 0.75 · route + hero try-on 1.25 · grid + segment + meter 0.5 · confirm + closed + card 0.5 · tests 0.5 ≈ 3.5. The 2.5 h cut: drop the in-place try-on (tap opens today's sheet) and the haul meter; keep the card, the route, the grid, the dialog.

stickyC.text:
C · Dress for the Night  (≈ 5 to 6 h, two sessions; not today)

What it is: the seasonal shelf is a fitting room, not a shelf. A look card on the wall opens a full-screen stage: Rosie on the set's background, a slot rail (hat · bow · held · mask · glasses · charm · aura · scene), a picker per slot; every tap dresses her at once, price tags hang off the unowned pieces, and one basket bar buys everything she is wearing (itemised ConfirmDialog, one atomic RPC). Bought pieces stay worn; a gold Share-the-look CTA posts a card to the sounder. After closes_at the pickers close and the look she kept stays.

Pillar fit: Collect at its strongest (you assemble, then you buy the assembly) and Connect for real (the share card is the set's marketing, from players). Risk: it is a second store grammar beside the shelf, and it tempts a 3,000-snout basket on a 1,840 balance.

Vs today: + a stage with multi-slot ephemeral equip (PigStage already resolves every slot; the state model is new), + slot rail and pickers, + basket math and partial-afford handling, + itemised dialog, + batch buy toast/celebration, + share card renderer. The set is also browsable only through slots (no grid), so a 16-piece set needs every slot drawn.

Server: A's tables plus buy_hats(hat_ids uuid[]) atomic (all-or-nothing, one balance check, one window check, returns remaining) and a share-card endpoint or on-device render. Winter = one shelf row, but every new slot category needs rail art.

Hours: migration + batch RPC 1.25 · stage + rail + pickers 2 · basket + dialog + celebration 1 · share card 1 · closed + tests 0.5 ≈ 5.75. Ship A or B now; C is what the shelf grows into once a set has a full look per pig.

rec.text:
Recommendation

Build A today. It fits the 2.5 h with the honest cut named, changes no grammar a player has learned since 2026-09-17, and its server shape (a seasonal_shelves row + shelf_key on hats) is the same one B and C stand on, so nothing is thrown away.

Fold in from B, if the clock allows: the stall card's countdown language ('leaving in 6 days') on the plank's kicker, and 'Yours · N' as the set sheet's third segment.

Save for the winter set: B's route with the in-place try-on, then C's basket once a set carries a whole look per pig.

Two rules to log in SKILL.md if A ships: (1) a seasonal piece is sold inside its window and nowhere else; a returning piece keeps its daily-drop life after the window. (2) the shelf is data: a winter set is a row and its hats, never a build.
